title: Sharp enrichment and its tensor and cotensor adjunctions
statement: Use marked simplicial sets, the markings $K^\flat,K^\sharp$, products and the internal Hom $H(X,Y)=Y^X$ of [lem-coef-marked-internal-hom]. For marked simplicial sets $X,Y$ put $$\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y),$$ with operators by restriction. These mapping simplicial sets give a simplicial enrichment of the category of marked simplicial sets: vertices are its morphisms, identities are their constant parameter families, and the composite of $f:X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y$ and $g:Y\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Z$ is $(x,t)\mapsto g(f(x,t),t)$. Composition is associative and unital. For every simplicial set $K$, the tensor and cotensor exist and are respectively $X\otimes K=X\times K^\sharp$ and $Y^K=H(K^\sharp,Y)$. More precisely, there are natural isomorphisms of simplicial sets $$\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(X\times K^\sharp,Y)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(X,Y))\cong\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(X,H(K^\sharp,Y)).$$ Here $\operatorname{Fun}(K,T)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K\times\Delta^n,T)$ for any simplicial set $T$. Both isomorphisms are the currying bijections, using the same marked map on $X\times K^\sharp\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ and interchanging its last two factors. They respect restriction, composition and identities. All constructions are relative to the input universe.

No Stacks tag states this marked-simplicial-set result. Sharp mapping composition and tensor/cotensor adjunctions underlying Corollary 3.1.4.4; no model-category assertion is made here.

proof.text: Write $T(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y)$. If $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the map $\Delta(\alpha):(\Delta^m)^\sharp\to(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ is marked, because every edge of both parameters is marked. Precomposition with $1_X\times\Delta(\alpha)$ defines the operator of $T(X,Y)$. The identity and composition rules for these operators follow from those for precomposition, so $T(X,Y)$ is a simplicial set. Since $\Delta^0$ has one simplex in each degree and its sole edge is degenerate, the projection $X\times(\Delta^0)^\sharp\to X$ is a marked isomorphism. Thus the vertices of $T(X,Y)$ are exactly the marked maps $X\to Y$.

proof.text: For $f\in T(X,Y)_n$ and $g\in T(Y,Z)_n$, form $X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Z$, with first map $(f,\operatorname{pr}_2)$ and second map $g$. The first map is marked: an edge $(e,t)$ is marked precisely when $e$ is marked in $X$, and then $f(e,t)$ is marked in $Y$ and $t$ is marked in the parameter. The resulting composite is $g(f(x,t),t)$. Restricting along $\alpha$ restricts both $f$ and $g$, so this gives a simplicial composition map. Both triple composites evaluate to $h(g(f(x,t),t),t)$; composing with the constant family $(x,t)\mapsto x$ evaluates to $f(x,t)$ on either side. This proves associativity and the unit laws, including the ordinary laws on vertices.

proof.text:
Here is the sharp-parameter currying calculation, for any simplicial set $L$. A marked map $a:X\times L^\sharp\to Y$ assigns to $\ell\in L_m$ the marked map $a\circ(1_X\times\ell):X\times(\Delta^m)^\sharp\to Y$, where $\ell$ denotes the simplex map. This is a simplicial map $b:L\to T(X,Y)$ by restriction. Conversely, given such a $b$, define $a_m(x,\ell)=(b_m(\ell))_m(x,\mathrm{id}_{[m]})$. For $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$, naturality of $b$ and of $b_m(\ell)$ gives
$$a_r(\alpha^*x,\alpha^*\ell)=(b_m(\ell))_r(\alpha^*x,\alpha)=\alpha^*a_m(x,\ell).$$
Thus $a$ is simplicial. For a marked edge $(e,\ell)$ of $X\times L^\sharp$, the edge $(e,\mathrm{id}_{[1]})$ of $X\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ is marked; its image under the marked map $b_1(\ell)$ is $a_1(e,\ell)$. Hence $a$ preserves markings.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph, printed p.154 (PDF page 172); sharp-parameter mapping property. Corollary 3.1.4.4, printed p.162 (PDF page 180), uses this enrichment. Both read online on 2026-10-17; the coordinate verifications are agent-written.

proof.text:
The two constructions in Step 3 are inverse. Starting with $a$ and evaluating its restriction at the identity simplex recovers $a_m(x,\ell)$. Starting with $b$, the recovered map associated to $\ell\in L_m$ has, at $x\in X_r$ and $\tau:[r]\to[m]$, value
$$a_r(x,\tau^*\ell)=(b_r(\tau^*\ell))_r(x,\mathrm{id}_{[r]})=(b_m(\ell))_r(x,\tau).$$
It is therefore exactly $b_m(\ell)$ in every degree. We obtain a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(X\times L^\sharp,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(L,T(X,Y))$. Its formulas commute with a map $L'\to L$, a marked map $X'\to X$, and a marked map $Y\to Y'$: each side respectively restricts $\ell$, substitutes for $x$, or postcomposes the displayed value. This also proves naturality, without a density or colimit theorem.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph, printed p.154 (PDF page 172); sharp-parameter mapping property. Corollary 3.1.4.4, printed p.162 (PDF page 180), uses this enrichment. Both read online on 2026-10-17; the coordinate verifications are agent-written.

proof.text:
Apply Step 4 with $L=K\times\Delta^n$. The marked sets $(K\times\Delta^n)^\sharp$ and $K^\sharp\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ agree, since an edge is marked on both sides regardless of its coordinates. Reassociating the products gives bijections
$$T(X\times K^\sharp,Y)_n\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K\times\Delta^n,T(X,Y))=\operatorname{Fun}(K,T(X,Y))_n.$$
Naturality in $L$ from Step 4, with the map $1_K\times\Delta(\alpha)$, proves compatibility with every simplicial operator in $n$. The inverse bijections have the same compatibility, so these degreewise bijections form the first required simplicial isomorphism. They exhibit $X\times K^\sharp$ as the tensor.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph, printed p.154 (PDF page 172); sharp-parameter mapping property. Corollary 3.1.4.4, printed p.162 (PDF page 180), uses this enrichment. Both read online on 2026-10-17; the coordinate verifications are agent-written.

proof.text:
Apply the exponential adjunction in [lem-coef-marked-internal-hom] to $Z=X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$, exponent $K^\sharp$, and target $Y$. It gives
$$T(X,H(K^\sharp,Y))_n\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}((X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp)\times K^\sharp,Y).$$
Interchanging the last two factors identifies the right side with $T(X\times K^\sharp,Y)_n$: both product markings require exactly that the $X$-edge be marked. The adjunction's naturality and this coordinate permutation commute with all restrictions in $n$. Combine this simplicial isomorphism with Step 5, reversing it where necessary, to obtain $\operatorname{Fun}(K,T(X,Y))\cong T(X,H(K^\sharp,Y))$. This exhibits $H(K^\sharp,Y)$ as the cotensor.

proof.text: The comparisons in Steps 5 and 6 use the same map on the three factors. Explicitly, if $a:X\times K^\sharp\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y$, its tensor transpose sends $(k,t)\in K_m\times(\Delta^n)_m$ to the map on $X\times(\Delta^m)^\sharp$ with value $(x,s)\mapsto a(x,s^*k,s^*t)$, for $s:[r]\to[m]$ and $x\in X_r$. Its cotensor transpose sends $(x,t)$ to the map $k\mapsto a(x,k,t)$ under the marked exponential adjunction. Consequently precomposition, postcomposition and parameter restriction on either description evaluate to exactly the same value of $a$. For composition of parameter families, both descriptions give $g(f(x,k,t),t)$; identities give the unchanged value. This verifies the stated compatibility with composition and identities. In particular, the tensor universal element sends $k$ to $(x\mapsto(x,k))$ and the cotensor universal element is evaluation $(k,h)\mapsto h(k)$; the two comparisons are induced by composition with these elements.

proof.text: All degreewise products, subsets of edges, sets of maps and the countably indexed simplicial families used above belong to the input Grothendieck universe. In particular, the marked internal Hom and its adjunction stay there by the last sentence of [lem-coef-marked-internal-hom]. The formulas make no fibrancy, nonemptiness or finiteness assumption on $X,Y,K$. For $K=\varnothing$, the tensor is empty and the cotensor is $H(\varnothing,Y)$, the terminal marked point; both sides of either adjunction are terminal simplicial sets. For $K=\Delta^0$, the tensor and cotensor reduce to $X$ and $Y$, and the comparisons reduce to the identity mapping object. Thus the same constructions include these edge cases and establish the universe assertion.
